hero.eyebrow: Training and placement partner for colleges
hero.title: From campus to career
hero.lead: RR Cloud Career Catalyst gives your students practical IT training, real software projects and placement support, and shows your college the progress of every batch.
hero.note: Placement support is provided within the agreed scope. Employment is not guaranteed.

landing.disclaimer: Placement support is provided within the agreed scope. Employment is not guaranteed.

forColleges.title: Built for colleges
forColleges.lead: An outside training partner, so your college does not need a large permanent team of specialists.

trainers.title: Practical, industry-oriented training
trainers.body: Taught by people with engineering experience, not exam coaching: Git, full-stack development, databases, testing and deployment.

projects.title: Real software projects
projects.body: Students work in teams on a working application, with code reviews and a final demonstration for your college.

reports.title: Reports you can rely on
reports.body: Attendance, assessments and projects are tracked for every batch, and outcomes are reported to your Training and Placement Officer.

howItWorks.title: How a programme runs
howItWorks.lead: The Career Ready programme over twelve weeks. Weeks and topics are adapted to each college.

baseline.title: Weeks 1–2: Baseline and fundamentals
baseline.body: A programming assessment, then problem-solving, Git and GitHub, HTML, CSS and JavaScript.

fullstack.title: Weeks 3–5: Full-stack development
fullstack.body: React or Vue, Node.js and Express, REST APIs, SQL or MongoDB, authentication and validation.

practices.title: Weeks 6–8: Engineering practices
practices.body: Testing, debugging, code reviews, secure coding basics, Docker and deployment.

project.title: Weeks 9–10: Team project
project.body: Students build, test and deploy a working application with requirements, issues, version control and documentation.

ai.title: Week 11: AI-assisted development
ai.body: Using coding assistants well: understanding generated code, testing AI output, privacy and responsible use.

career.title: Week 12: Career readiness
career.body: Coding tests, resume reviews, mock technical interviews, project presentations and individual feedback.

howItWorks.note: Where programming fundamentals are weak, we begin with a foundation module first.

programmes.title: Programmes
programmes.lead: Start with one batch, agree what will be measured, and grow from the results.
programmes.note: Scope, student numbers and dates are agreed in writing with each college. Request a proposal for the programme that fits.

skill_builder.name: Skill Builder
skill_builder.body: An introductory engagement: 20–30 hours of workshops on Git, programming fundamentals and web development or AI coding tools, with a mini project, a basic assessment and an attendance report.

career_ready.name: Career Ready
career_ready.body: Structured full-stack or Python training, a team project with code reviews and demonstrations, aptitude and resume preparation, mock interviews and a final student readiness report.

campus_partner.name: Campus Career Partner
campus_partner.body: Several training batches through the year, final-year project mentoring, a placement-readiness calendar, assessments and mock interviews, and regular progress reviews with your Training and Placement Officer.

outcomes.title: Measured, not promised
outcomes.lead: Before training starts we agree with your college what will be measured and how. These are the targets we propose for a pilot.
outcomes.note: Targets are adjusted to student readiness and the agreed scope. They are suggested measures, not promises of job placement.

placement.label: Placement reporting
placement.value: Applications, interviews, offers and joining tracked separately

progress.title: See progress as it happens
progress.lead: Trainers record attendance, assignments, projects and mock interviews. Your Training and Placement Officer and administrators follow each batch in the Career Catalyst portal, and students see their own progress.

items.placement: Placement applications, interviews, offers and joining

items.report: A batch report you can download as a PDF

placement.title: Placement support
placement.lead: Preparing students and connecting them with relevant employers, step by step.

steps.assess: Assess students and group them by skill level
steps.prepare: Prepare resumes, GitHub profiles and project portfolios
steps.match: Identify employers whose entry-level roles match the students
steps.coordinate: Coordinate applications, interviews and recruitment drives
steps.track: Track interviews, feedback, offers and joining
steps.report: Report verified outcomes to the college

placement.network: We are building a focused network of relevant employers rather than promising access to a large one.

who.a: Colleges and institutes with BCA, MCA, B.Tech, B.Sc. Computer Science, polytechnic and similar programmes.

length.a: Skill Builder runs for 2–4 weeks and Career Ready for 8–12 weeks. Campus Career Partner is an annual agreement.

need.q: What do you need from the college?
need.a: Classroom or lab access, internet and a named coordinator.

cost.a: Fees depend on the programme, the batch size and the scope. Request a proposal and we will send a written quote.

pilot.a: Yes. You can begin with a Skill Builder or a single Career Ready batch, agree the measures up front and review the results before going further.

jobs.a: No. We help with preparation, employer outreach and tracking within the agreed scope. Employment is not guaranteed.

footer.by: A programme of Rural Root Cloud Tech Services & Training.
